stops.stop: Rehovot, the fixed points of recursive definitions
stops.date_confidence: Contradiction left standing. The Mathematics Genealogy Project (id 19271) and the current Wikipedia article both date the Weizmann PhD to 1977, advisor Zohar Manna, dissertation 'The Fixed Points Of Recursive Definitions'; 1976 appears in the record as the year the thesis work and its technical report are dated. This stop is pinned to the thesis year, 1976, because the Warwick postdoc that follows begins in 1976; the degree year is very likely 1977. Month and day are defaults.

stops.stop: Coventry, the year with Mike Paterson
stops.date_confidence: The University of Warwick's own Department of Computer Science states that Shamir has been known there since 1976, when he spent a year as a post-doc with Mike Paterson, and that he went directly to MIT afterwards. Month and day are defaults. This crowds the record hard: the RSA construction is dated to April 1977 at MIT, which leaves the Warwick year at most seven or eight months, and other summaries date the MIT start variously to 1977 and to 1978. The contradiction is recorded, not resolved.
